topic: How do GEO and LEO orbital altitudes impact link budget calculations for Ka vs S-band deployments in 5G satcom?
consensus_response: The distinct characteristics of GEO and LEO constellations significantly impact link budget calculations for Ka- and S-band deployments in 5G satcom. LEO satellites, at 500-2000 km altitude, offer reduced propagation delays and lower atmospheric interference, enhancing signal strength and capacity. However, frequent satellite handovers increase intra-satellite interference and require more frequent uplink timing adjustments. In contrast, GEO satellites at 35,786 km provide consistent signal strength, but longer delays and higher atmospheric attenuation affect Ka-band more than S-band due to higher frequencies. The optimal choice of Ka or S-band depends on the specific 5G satcom application and design requirements, considering the trade-offs between signal strength, capacity, and latency.
